decision: scoped the Mac and Linux port to hotkeys, sounds, finding Azahar, the instance lock, prompts, updater and packages
why: the user wants real Mac and Linux players to try it

decision: left the settings dialog and pa3ds's own window Windows-only
why: they are Win32 dialog templates; a Mac or Linux player edits user/config.toml

decision: Linux speech goes through speech-dispatcher, not Orca's D-Bus backend
why: Orca's backend needs giomm-2.68 at run time, which most desktops lack and without which pa3ds would not start

decision: replayed all 162 tapes on the untouched tree as label rust-base
why: Windows must behave the same after the shared key and audio code changes

decision: split the work into four units by file: keys, platform (Azahar, paths, lock), audio, release (prompts, updater, packages, manual)
why: the files do not overlap, so four agents can work at once and merge cleanly
evidence: scratchpad os-port-common.md; branches os/keys os/platform os/audio os/release

decision: keys share one decision function across Windows, a macOS event tap and a Linux X11 grab, in Windows key codes
why: one set of rules for which keys pa3ds takes, so the three cannot drift apart

decision: one cpal output behind both waveout modules, resampling to the device's rate
why: callers stay unchanged; macOS devices rarely take 22050 Hz

decision: merged os/release: osascript and zenity prompts, the updater per platform, tools/package.sh and release jobs
why: its own 11 tests pass on macOS and Linux and the release run made all three packages

decision: moved the Linux build from Ubuntu 24.04 to 22.04
why: a 24.04 binary needs glibc 2.39 and would not start on Debian 12 or Ubuntu 22.04

decision: merged os/keys: one key decision for the Windows hook, a macOS event tap and Linux X11 grabs
why: read the Windows path line by line against the old hook: same calls in the same order, SYS messages folded as track already did
